_about: The offerings side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of offering and sacrifice that more than one book shares, from Abel and Abraham and the Law's offerings to the psalms, the prophets and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: A pleasing aroma

The Law & history: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma
a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD
the food for My food offerings, as a pleasing aroma to Me
I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices
Psalms & wisdom: I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams
The Prophets: you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you
I will accept you as a pleasing aroma
The letters: gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God
They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God
we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ

rows.alike: In the Law a burnt offering is 'a pleasing aroma to the LORD' (Leviticus 1:9), and Genesis 8:21 has 'When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma'; Ephesians 5:2 says Christ 'gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God', and Philippians 4:18 calls gifts received from Epaphroditus 'a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice'.
rows.different: The aroma can be refused: 'I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices' (Leviticus 26:31), and Ezekiel 16:19 has 'you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you'. In Ezekiel 20:41 God says 'I will accept you as a pleasing aroma', and in 2 Corinthians 2:15 'we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ'.

rows.title: Without blemish

The Law & history: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male
he is to present an unblemished male
it must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable
an unblemished red heifer that has no defect
he is to present an unblemished male
he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering
must offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats
Psalms & wisdom: you will lift up your face without blemish
The Prophets: an unblemished male goat as a sin offering
six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram
sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord
The letters: the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot
without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish, but holy and blameless
to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence
to present you unblemished in His glorious presence

rows.alike: The Law asks that an offering be 'without blemish or defect to be acceptable' (Leviticus 22:21), 'an unblemished male' (Leviticus 1:10; 22:19), or 'an unblemished male goat' (Leviticus 4:23); 1 Peter 1:19 speaks of 'the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot', and Hebrews 9:14 says Christ 'offered Himself unblemished to God'.
rows.different: In Malachi 1:14 the one who 'sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord' is called 'cursed'. Ephesians 5:27, Colossians 1:22 and Jude 1:24 use the word of people: 'without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish' (Ephesians 5:27), 'to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence' (Colossians 1:22), 'to present you unblemished in His glorious presence' (Jude 1:24).

rows.title: The blood is the life: do not eat it

The Law & history: you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it
the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life
the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it
The Prophets: You eat meat with the blood in it
Gospels & Acts: from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood
they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood

rows.alike: The Law forbids eating 'meat with its lifeblood still in it' (Genesis 9:4) and gives the reason 'the blood is the life' (Deuteronomy 12:23); 1 Samuel 14:33 and Ezekiel 33:25 name the same act, eating 'meat with the blood', and Acts 15:29 and 21:25 have 'abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood', the second of 'the Gentile believers'.
rows.different: Leviticus 17:14 adds 'whoever eats it must be cut off', and 1 Samuel 14:33 calls eating meat with the blood 'sinning against the LORD'. In Acts 15:20 'from blood' stands in a list beside 'food polluted by idols' and 'the meat of strangled animals'.

rows.title: It is the blood that makes atonement

The Law & history: I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul
The letters: nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith
by making peace through the blood of His cross
the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin

rows.alike: Leviticus 17:11 says 'it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul'; Hebrews 9:22 says 'without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness', and Romans 3:25 speaks of 'an atoning sacrifice in His blood'.
rows.different: Leviticus 17:11 says 'I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar'; the letters say 'purified with blood' (Hebrews 9:22), 'making peace through the blood of His cross' (Colossians 1:20) and 'the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin' (1 John 1:7).

rows.title: To make atonement

The Law & history: the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven
on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you
when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven
Psalms & wisdom: deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name
By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for
The Prophets: Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for
to make atonement for the house of Israel
to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity
The letters: a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people
He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins
sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins

rows.alike: In the Law 'the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven' (Leviticus 4:20); Hebrews 2:17 uses the same words of 'a merciful and faithful high priest', 'to make atonement for the sins of the people', and Daniel 9:24 has 'to make atonement for iniquity'.
rows.different: Who atones differs: 'the priest' in Leviticus, God in the Psalms ('You atone for our transgressions', Psalm 65:3), and in Proverbs 16:6 'loving devotion and faithfulness'. In Isaiah 6:7 it happens when 'this has touched your lips'; 1 John 2:2 and 4:10 use the noun, 'the atoning sacrifice for our sins'.

rows.title: By His blood: purchased, redeemed, released

Gospels & Acts: the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood
The letters: we have now been justified by His blood
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses
He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption
it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed
to sanctify the people by His own blood
Revelation: To Him who loves us and has released us from our sins by His blood
by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb

rows.alike: Acts 20:28 and Revelation 5:9 both say people were 'purchased' with His blood: 'which He purchased with His own blood', 'by Your blood You purchased for God'. Ephesians 1:7 and Hebrews 9:12 both speak of 'redemption' by His blood.
rows.different: Each names what the blood does in its own word: 'justified' (Romans 5:9), 'the forgiveness of our trespasses' (Ephesians 1:7), 'released us from our sins' (Revelation 1:5), 'conquered him' (Revelation 12:11), 'to sanctify the people' (Hebrews 13:12). What is purchased is 'the church of God' in Acts 20:28 and people 'from every tribe and tongue and people and nation' in Revelation 5:9.

rows.title: The blood of bulls and goats

The Law & history: He is to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar
Psalms & wisdom: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
The Prophets: I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats
The letters: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves
it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins
the blood of goats and bulls

rows.alike: Each speaks of the blood of bulls or goats: 'the blood of goats' (Psalm 50:13), 'the blood of bulls and lambs and goats' (Isaiah 1:11), 'the blood of bulls and goats' (Hebrews 10:4); in Leviticus 16:18 'the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood' are put 'on all the horns of the altar'.
rows.different: In Leviticus 16:18 the blood is put 'on all the horns of the altar'. In Psalm 50:13 God asks 'Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?', and in Isaiah 1:11 He says 'I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats'. Hebrews 9:13 has 'the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean'; Hebrews 10:4 has 'it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins'; and Hebrews 9:12 has 'He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves'.

rows.title: Each day, once a year, once for all

The Law & history: This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old
to make atonement once a year for the Israelites because of all their sins
Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar
The Prophets: an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning
It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice
The letters: He does not need to offer daily sacrifices
He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself
only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood
He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself
the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all
Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices
The death He died, He died to sin once for all
Christ also suffered for sins once for all

rows.alike: The Law sets offerings 'each day' (Exodus 29:38) and atonement 'once a year' (Leviticus 16:34; Exodus 30:10); Hebrews names the same measures: 'daily sacrifices' (7:27), 'once a year' (9:7) and 'Day after day' (10:11).
rows.different: Among these verses the words 'once for all' appear only in the letters: 'He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself' (Hebrews 7:27), 'the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all' (Hebrews 10:10), 'The death He died, He died to sin once for all' (Romans 6:10), 'Christ also suffered for sins once for all' (1 Peter 3:18); Hebrews 9:26 has 'He has appeared once for all'. Ezekiel 46:13 has 'an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning', and in Daniel 8:11 'It magnified itself' and 'removed His daily sacrifice'.

rows.title: The Passover lamb

The Law & history: select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb
when I see the blood, I will pass over you
It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD
You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice
the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month
the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles
Gospels & Acts: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed
the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed
The letters: For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood

rows.alike: The phrase 'the Passover lamb' runs from Exodus 12:21, 'slaughter the Passover lamb', through 2 Chronicles 35:1 and Ezra 6:20 to Mark 14:12 and Luke 22:7, where 'the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed'; 1 Corinthians 5:7 says 'Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed'.
rows.different: Exodus 12:27 calls it 'the Passover sacrifice to the LORD'; the Gospels name the day it 'was to be sacrificed'; among these verses only 1 Corinthians 5:7 names a person as 'our Passover lamb'. Hebrews 11:28 says 'By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood', and Exodus 12:13 has 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you'.

rows.title: Abraham offered Isaac on the altar

The Law & history: Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains
He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood
He split the wood for a burnt offering
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac
The letters: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar
Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

rows.alike: Genesis 22:9 tells how Abraham 'placed him on the altar'; Hebrews 11:17 and James 2:21 both say he 'offered' Isaac 'on the altar'.
rows.different: Genesis 22:2 gives God's command, 'Offer him there as a burnt offering'. Hebrews 11:17 says 'By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar' and calls Isaac 'his one and only son'; James 2:21 says 'our father Abraham' offered his son Isaac on the altar.

rows.title: Abel's offering and Cain's

The Law & history: the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering
but He had no regard for Cain and his offering
The letters: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts.

rows.alike: Both set Abel's offering against Cain's: 'the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering' (Genesis 4:4); 'Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did' (Hebrews 11:4).
rows.different: Genesis 4:4-5 says the LORD 'looked with favor on Abel and his offering' and 'had no regard for Cain and his offering'; Hebrews 11:4 says 'By faith' and that Abel 'was commended as righteous'.

rows.title: A sin offering, a guilt offering

The Law & history: a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed
he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed
the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering
Take for yourself a young bull for a sin offering
with a young bull for a sin offering
you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering
The Prophets: when His soul is made a guilt offering
a young bull from the herd as a sin offering
you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering
The letters: God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin
And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.
If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains

rows.alike: Leviticus has 'a sin offering' (4:3) and 'his guilt offering' (5:6); Isaiah 53:10 has 'when His soul is made a guilt offering', and Romans 8:3 has God 'sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin'.
rows.different: Isaiah 53:10 uses the word of 'His soul', and Romans 8:3 of God's 'own Son'. Ezekiel 43:19 and 43:25 have 'a young bull from the herd as a sin offering' and 'a male goat daily for a sin offering'. Hebrews 10:18 says 'And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed', and Hebrews 10:26 says 'If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains'.

rows.title: Outside the camp

The Law & history: burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering
he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it
whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp
he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence
The Prophets: take away the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the appointed part of the temple area outside the sanctuary
The letters: the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp
Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood
let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore

rows.alike: The Law burns the sin offering's body 'outside the camp' when its blood has been 'brought into the Most Holy Place' (Leviticus 16:27); Hebrews 13:11 has both, 'the blood of animals into the Holy Place' and 'the bodies are burned outside the camp'.
rows.different: Ezekiel 43:21 has 'outside the sanctuary'. Hebrews 13:12 says Jesus 'suffered outside the city gate', and 13:13 calls its readers to 'go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore'.

rows.title: Sprinkled: blood, water, the ashes of a heifer

The Law & history: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the skin disease
sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat
gather up the ashes of the heifer
The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person
The Prophets: so He will sprinkle many nations
I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean
The letters: the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean
he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship
having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience
the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel
for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood

rows.alike: Numbers 19:9 gathers 'the ashes of the heifer', and Hebrews 9:13 names 'the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean'; the Law sprinkles 'the one to be cleansed' (Leviticus 14:7), and Hebrews 10:22 speaks of 'hearts sprinkled to cleanse us'.
rows.different: In the Law the one to be cleansed is sprinkled (Leviticus 14:7; Numbers 19:19) and blood is sprinkled 'on the east side of the mercy seat' (Leviticus 16:14); Ezekiel 36:25 has God say 'I will also sprinkle clean water on you'; Isaiah 52:15 has 'He will sprinkle many nations'. In Hebrews 10:22 it is 'hearts' that are sprinkled, 'from a guilty conscience', and Hebrews 12:24 and 1 Peter 1:2 speak of 'sprinkled blood' and 'sprinkling by His blood'.

rows.title: With hyssop

The Law & history: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin
two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the one to be cleansed
take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent
the hyssop growing in the wall
Psalms & wisdom: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean
Gospels & Acts: they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop
The letters: he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people

rows.alike: Hyssop is what blood or water is put on with: 'dip it into the blood' (Exodus 12:22), 'dip it in the water, and sprinkle' (Numbers 19:18), 'water, scarlet wool, and hyssop' (Hebrews 9:19); Psalm 51:7 prays 'Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean'.
rows.different: Psalm 51:7 has 'Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow'. Leviticus 14:4 and Hebrews 9:19 add scarlet: 'scarlet yarn', 'scarlet wool'.

rows.title: Thank offerings and the sacrifice of praise

The Law & history: along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil
come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD
sacrificed peace offerings and thank offerings on it
Psalms & wisdom: Sacrifice a thank offering to God
He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me
Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing
I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the LORD
I will render thank offerings to You
The Prophets: and thank offerings to the house of the LORD
the voices of those bringing thank offerings into the house of the LORD
But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You
that we may present the fruit of our lips
The letters: let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name

rows.alike: Leviticus 7:12 has 'the sacrifice of thanksgiving'; the Psalms have 'a sacrifice of thanksgiving' (Psalm 116:17), and Jonah has 'with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You'; Hebrews 13:15 has 'a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips', as Hosea 14:2 has 'the fruit of our lips'.
rows.different: In Leviticus 7:12 it comes with 'unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil'; in the Psalms it goes with words, 'declare His works' and 'call on the name of the LORD'; in Hebrews 13:15 it is offered 'continually' and is 'the fruit of lips that confess His name'.

rows.title: A broken spirit, a contrite heart

Psalms & wisdom: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit
The Prophets: I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite
This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word

rows.alike: The shared word is 'contrite', with 'spirit' or 'heart': 'a broken and a contrite heart' (Psalm 51:17), 'the contrite in spirit' (Psalm 34:18), 'humble and contrite in spirit' (Isaiah 66:2), 'the heart of the contrite' (Isaiah 57:15).
rows.different: Only Psalm 51:17 calls it a sacrifice: 'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit'. Psalm 34:18 says 'The LORD is near'; Isaiah 57:15 has God say 'I dwell' with them; Isaiah 66:2 'This is the one I will esteem'.

rows.title: Sacrifices of righteousness

The Law & history: They will call the peoples to a mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness
Psalms & wisdom: Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD
Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar
The Prophets: He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver. Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness

rows.alike: Each joins sacrifice to righteousness: 'sacrifices of righteousness' (Deuteronomy 33:19), 'the sacrifices of the righteous' (Psalm 4:5), 'righteous sacrifices' (Psalm 51:19), 'offerings to the LORD in righteousness' (Malachi 3:3).
rows.different: Psalm 4:5 is a command, 'Offer'. Deuteronomy 33:19, Psalm 51:19 and Malachi 3:3 speak of what will be: 'there they will offer', 'Then You will delight', 'Then they will present', Malachi's after He will 'purify the sons of Levi'.

rows.title: Better than sacrifice

The Law & history: Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice
Psalms & wisdom: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice
Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools
I will praise God's name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving
And this will please the LORD more than an ox
The Prophets: I did not merely command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices
but this is what I commanded them: Obey Me
Gospels & Acts: to love your neighbor as yourself. This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices

rows.alike: Each sets something above sacrifice in a comparison: 'obedience is better than sacrifice' (1 Samuel 15:22), 'more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice' (Proverbs 21:3), 'more than an ox' (Psalm 69:31), 'more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices' (Mark 12:33).
rows.different: What is set higher differs: 'obedience to His voice' (1 Samuel 15:22) and 'Obey Me' (Jeremiah 7:23), 'righteousness and justice' (Proverbs 21:3), 'to listen' (Ecclesiastes 5:1), praise 'with thanksgiving' (Psalm 69:30), and in Mark 12:33 the love of God and 'your neighbor as yourself'.

rows.title: Sacrifice and offering You did not desire

The Law & history: Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice
Psalms & wisdom: Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but my ears You have opened. Burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not require.
For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
The Prophets: What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?
Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
The letters: when Christ came into the world, He said
Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me
In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.
although they are offered according to the law

rows.alike: 'Sacrifice and offering You did not desire' stands word for word in Psalm 40:6 and Hebrews 10:5; Psalm 51:16 'You do not delight in sacrifice' and Hebrews 10:6 'You took no delight' share the word 'delight'; Micah 6:8 asks 'what does the LORD require of you', where Psalm 40:6 says of burnt offerings 'You did not require'.
rows.different: Psalm 40:6 has 'my ears You have opened' where Hebrews 10:5 has 'a body You prepared for Me'; Hebrews 10:5 gives the words to Christ, 'when Christ came into the world, He said', and 10:8 has the note 'although they are offered according to the law'. Micah 6:8 has 'to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God'.

rows.title: I will not accept them

The Law & history: You must not present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf
Psalms & wisdom: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable-how much more so when brought with ill intent!
The Prophets: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me
Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me
although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them
Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them
whatever they offer there is defiled
I will accept no offering from your hands
You bring offerings that are stolen, lame, or sick! Should I accept these from your hands?
He no longer regards your offerings or receives them gladly from your hands

rows.alike: Jeremiah 14:12 and Amos 5:22 say the same words of 'burnt offerings and grain offerings': 'I will not accept them'; Malachi 1:10 has 'I will accept no offering from your hands'. Proverbs 15:8 and 21:27 say 'The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable', and Isaiah 1:13 'your incense is detestable to Me'.
rows.different: Leviticus 22:20 gives the animal's 'defect' as the reason, and Malachi 1:13 offerings 'stolen, lame, or sick'; Proverbs names 'the wicked' and 'ill intent'. Jeremiah 14:12 and Amos 5:22 give no reason within the verse.

rows.title: Accepted, pleasing to God

The Law & history: so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him
in order for it to be accepted on your behalf
The Prophets: Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar
Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD
The letters: to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God
offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ
do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased

rows.alike: The Law's words are 'accepted on his behalf' and 'accepted on your behalf' (Leviticus 1:4; 22:19), and Isaiah 56:7 has 'will be accepted on My altar'; the letters have 'pleasing to God' (Romans 12:1), 'acceptable to God' (1 Peter 2:5), 'God is pleased' (Hebrews 13:16).
rows.different: In the Law and the Prophets what is accepted is an animal or an offering, and in Ezekiel 43:27 God says 'I will accept you'. In the letters the sacrifices are 'your bodies' (Romans 12:1), 'spiritual sacrifices' (1 Peter 2:5), and 'to do good and to share with others' (Hebrews 13:16).

rows.title: Poured out like a drink offering

The Law & history: he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil
Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area
a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine
nor are you to pour a drink offering on it
a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering
a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering
half a hin of wine as a drink offering
as well as a drink offering
Psalms & wisdom: Sorrows will multiply to those who chase other gods. I will not pour out their libations of blood
The Prophets: they pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Me to anger
Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD
you have poured out a drink offering
The letters: even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith

rows.different: Exodus 30:9 says 'nor are you to pour a drink offering on it'; Jeremiah 7:18 has 'they pour out drink offerings to other gods', and Psalm 16:4 'I will not pour out their libations of blood'; Joel 1:9 says 'Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD'.
